domain: SAP enterprise resource planning (ERP) and financial settlement processing
summary:
This enterprise reference application contains company-scoped sales, purchasing, inventory, quality, production, finance and integration workflows. Business roles create and release orders, receive and inspect goods, manage stock and picking, invoice shipments, record payments and reconcile bank files. It also includes effective-dated pricing, returns with credit notes, operational incident handling and analytical source code.

Inbound IDoc, SOAP delivery and payment-event adapters use explicit external identifiers and business authorization. The external settlement job reconciles invoices with bank CSV. In this target, ten qualified ABAP calculations have generated HANA SQLScript/AMDP counterparts, and the settlement job uses .NET 10 OAuth/OData.

This is a model-derived map reviewed against repository implementations. Source code, declared contracts and locally tested behavior are distinct evidence scopes. Native SAP activation, native HANA execution and deployed external connectivity remain unverified; local validation details are recorded separately.

useCases.title: Create and manage sales orders
useCases.description: Sales representatives create new customer orders, validate order details, and track order status. The system captures customer information, line items, pricing, and delivery requirements.
steps: Sales representative enters customer order details
System validates customer credit status and material availability
Order is saved to the database with unique order ID
Order items are recorded with pricing and delivery dates
useCases.evidence: createOrder function validates customer blocking status, processes 1-100 order lines with material/plant validation, calculates total from unitPrice*quantity, and writes to SalesOrders and SalesOrderItems entities

useCases.title: Release order for fulfillment
useCases.description: Warehouse managers release approved sales orders to begin picking and shipping. The system validates company and order authorization, reserves inventory atomically with credit checks, and logs the release event.
steps: Warehouse manager selects order for release
System checks company authorization and order validity
Credit limit is verified and customer exposure is increased atomically
Inventory is reserved for each order item with availability checks
Order status is updated to 'Released'
Release event is logged to audit and integration outbox
useCases.evidence: releaseOrder function performs atomic state transition with predicates (status='DRAFT', revision match), updates BusinessPartners exposure with credit-limit check, reserves Stock with available-quantity guards, writes Reservations, CreditDecisions, AuditEvents, and IntegrationEvents in one transaction

useCases.title: Cancel sales orders
useCases.description: Sales representatives cancel orders that are in draft or released state. The system reverses stock reservations and customer credit exposure if the order was already released.
steps: Sales representative selects order for cancellation
System validates order revision and company access
Order status is transitioned to 'Cancelled'
If order was released, stock reservations are reversed to available inventory
Customer credit exposure is reduced by the order total
useCases.evidence: cancelOrder function checks expectedRevision, transitions from DRAFT or RELEASED to CANCELLED, reverses Reservations with Stock available/reserved adjustments, and reduces BusinessPartners exposure atomically

useCases.title: Deliver goods to customer
useCases.description: Logistics coordinators confirm outbound deliveries and ship goods to customers. The system integrates with external logistics systems via SOAP to confirm delivery status and update order fulfillment.
steps: Logistics coordinator receives order release notification
System processes SOAP ConfirmDelivery message from external logistics system
Delivery confirmation is validated against order and company scope
Order status is updated to shipped
Delivery event is recorded in audit and integration ledger
useCases.evidence: confirmDelivery processes SOAP Envelope with ConfirmDelivery operation, validates CompanyCode scope, resolves external OrderNumber to internal orderID via ExternalIdentifiers, generates idempotent requestID from SOAP MessageID hash, and calls shipOrder function

useCases.title: Create and approve purchase orders
useCases.description: Buyers create company-scoped purchase orders with validated suppliers, materials, plants, quantities and prices. A different PurchasingManager actor approves a draft order; the CAP implementation does not provide a budget-routing workflow.
steps: Validate supplier, organizational scope and purchase lines
Create a draft order and its line items transactionally
Reject approval by the creator
Record approval by a different authorized actor
useCases.evidence: createPurchaseOrder validates Suppliers blocked status, processes items with Materials/Plants checks, calculates total from quantity*unitPrice, writes PurchaseOrders (status DRAFT) and PurchaseOrderItems; approvePurchaseOrder enforces createdByActor != user.id, transitions from DRAFT to APPROVED; ZCL_PO_APPROVAL_POLICY.EVALUATE enforces segregation-of-duties and approval authority limits

useCases.title: Receive goods from supplier
useCases.description: Warehouse clerks record goods receipts for approved purchase orders and create quality inspection lots. The system validates received quantity against outstanding order quantity and updates purchase order status.
steps: Warehouse clerk receives goods and enters receipt quantity and batch
System validates purchase order is approved for receipt
Received quantity is checked against outstanding order quantity
Quality inspection lot is created with status 'OPEN'
Goods receipt record is created linking to the inspection lot
Purchase order status is updated to 'RECEIVED' or 'PARTIALLY_RECEIVED'
useCases.evidence: receiveGoods validates order status (APPROVED or PARTIALLY_RECEIVED), updates PurchaseOrderItems receivedQuantity with atomic predicate (receivedQuantity + quantity <= order quantity), creates QualityLots (status OPEN) and GoodsReceipts, updates PurchaseOrders status based on whether all items are fully received

useCases.title: Process supplier quality inspections
useCases.description: Quality inspectors record bounded sample measurements and defect counts against the material quality policy. Accepted lots release stock; rejected lots remain quarantined.
steps: Quality inspector receives supplier inspection lot
Inspector records sample size, defective count, and characteristic measurements
System evaluates quality policy: defect rate basis points and characteristic bounds
If inspection passes, stock is released to unrestricted use and added to available inventory
If inspection fails, lot is quarantined and stock is blocked
Quality findings are recorded with pass/fail status for each characteristic
useCases.evidence: inspectLot validates QualityLots, checks sampled/defective against lot quantity, retrieves QualityPolicies maxDefectBasisPoints, evaluates findings array (characteristic bounds passed), calculates acceptance using defective*10000 <= sampled*maxDefectBasisPoints, transitions lot to ACCEPTED or REJECTED, writes QualityFindings, and updates Stock available quantity if accepted; ZCL_QUALITY_POLICY.EVALUATE enforces defect rate and sample validation

useCases.title: Generate and track invoices
useCases.description: Billing clerks generate customer invoices based on shipped orders. The system calculates invoice amounts, applies tax policy based on customer country, and creates draft journal entries for revenue recognition.
steps: Billing clerk selects shipped order for invoicing
System retrieves customer country and validates tax policy is effective
Invoice amount is calculated from order total; tax is calculated using rateBasisPoints
Invoice is created with unique ID, net amount, tax amount, and due date
Order status is updated to 'INVOICED'
Draft journal entry is created with debit/credit lines for accounts receivable, revenue, and tax payable
useCases.evidence: invoiceOrder validates order status (SHIPPED), retrieves TaxPolicies by customer country and order currency, calculates net and tax using (net*rateBasisPoints+5000)/10000 integer arithmetic, transitions SalesOrders to INVOICED, creates Invoices (status OPEN), creates draft JournalEntries with JournalLines for accounts 110000 (debit A/R), 400000 (credit revenue), and 220000 (credit tax)

useCases.title: Process customer payments
useCases.description: Accountants record partial or final payments against an open company-scoped invoice. The transaction validates currency and unique bank reference, prevents overpayment, updates the invoice and releases customer exposure when fully paid; it does not create a cash-account journal.
steps: Validate invoice, company, currency, amount and bank reference
Atomically update the paid amount and record the payment
Keep partial payments open or mark the invoice paid
Release customer exposure once on full settlement
useCases.evidence: settlePayment validates Invoices status OPEN, checks currency match, verifies Payments bankReference uniqueness, calculates paid+amount using cents (BigInt minor units), atomically updates Invoices paidAmount and status (PAID if next==total), reduces BusinessPartners exposure on full payment, writes Payments record; ZCL_PAYMENT_POLICY.EVALUATE enforces currency match and amount bounds

useCases.title: Process payment events from external systems
useCases.description: Finance analysts receive payment notifications from external banking systems via CloudEvents. The system validates the event contract, resolves external invoice references to internal IDs, and applies payments to open invoices.
steps: Payment CloudEvent is received from external banking system
System validates CloudEvents 1.0 specification and type 'enterprise.payment.received.v1'
External invoice number is resolved to internal invoice ID via ExternalIdentifiers mapping
Payment is applied to invoice using settlePayment logic
Event is deduplicated using content hash of CloudEvent ID and source
useCases.evidence: receivePayment parses CloudEvent JSON, validates specversion/type/datacontenttype, checks source matches sourceSystem and data.companyCode matches envelope.companyCode, resolves data.invoiceNumber to invoiceID via resolve function (ExternalIdentifiers lookup), generates idempotent requestID from event source/company/id hash, calls settlePayment

useCases.title: Reconcile bank transactions to invoices
useCases.description: Finance analysts run periodic settlement batch jobs to reconcile bank transaction CSV files against the open invoice ledger retrieved via OAuth-secured OData API. The system validates payment amounts, matches transactions to invoices, and generates reconciliation reports with outcome codes.
steps: Settlement batch job reads bank transaction CSV file with header validation
System retrieves open invoice ledger via OAuth-secured Finance API with pagination
System validates all returned data is within requested company/currency/date scope
Payments are matched to invoices based on invoice reference and amount
System calculates expected, received, and difference for each invoice
Outcome codes are assigned: MATCHED, UNDERPAID, OVERPAID, MISSING_PAYMENT, UNMATCHED_BANK
Reconciliation report is generated with totals and mismatch count
Report is stored with content-addressed filename (SHA256 hash prevents overwrites)
useCases.evidence: SettlementJob.RunAsync validates scope, calls BankCsvReader.Read (validates CSV header, parses rows, enforces 100k limit, validates amounts and dates), calls ApiInvoiceLedger.ReadOpenAsync (OAuth bearer token, OData $filter on companyCode/currency/dueDate/status, pagination with visited set, 8MB page limit, validates returned scope matches request), calls Reconciler.Run (ValidateScope regex, builds ledger dictionary with duplicate/scope checks, aggregates bank payments by invoiceId, calculates expected-received difference, assigns outcome based on tolerance, returns ReconciliationReport); ReportStore.SaveAsync writes JSON with SHA256 filename, atomic move with content comparison on collision

useCases.title: Reserve inventory for orders
useCases.description: Warehouse planners reserve inventory stock for sales orders. The system checks available stock, creates reservations, and updates stock levels atomically. Reservations are created during order release workflow.
steps: Order release workflow initiates inventory reservation
System checks available stock at the plant for each material
Stock reservation is created for the required quantity with atomic predicate
Available stock is reduced and reserved stock is increased
Reservation record is tracked with status 'RESERVED'
useCases.evidence: releaseOrder function (order-workflow.js) updates Stock with atomic predicates: available -= quantity, reserved += quantity, revision += 1, WHERE available >= quantity; writes Reservations with status RESERVED; cancelOrder reverses the operation with symmetric predicates

useCases.title: Transfer inventory between plants
useCases.description: Warehouse planners transfer inventory stock between plants within the same company. The system validates plant ownership, atomically reduces stock at source plant and increases at destination plant, and records the movement.
steps: Warehouse planner initiates stock transfer between two plants
System validates both plants belong to the same company
Available stock is reduced at source plant with atomic availability check
Available stock is increased at destination plant (created if not exists)
Stock movement record is created with reason 'TRANSFER'
useCases.evidence: transferStock validates fromPlant != toPlant, checks both Plants exist for companyCode, atomically updates Stock available at fromPlant (WHERE available >= quantity), updates or inserts Stock at toPlant, writes StockMovements with fromPlant/toPlant/quantity/reason

useCases.title: Count and adjust inventory
useCases.description: Inventory controllers perform physical stock counts and adjust inventory records to match actual quantities. The system validates counted quantity does not discard committed reservations and updates available stock with revision tracking.
steps: Inventory controller performs physical count and enters counted quantity
System validates stock revision matches expected (no concurrent changes)
System enforces counted quantity >= reserved (cannot discard commitments)
Available stock is calculated as counted - reserved
Stock is updated with new revision number
Stock movement is recorded with adjustment reason
useCases.evidence: countStock validates countedQuantity and reason, retrieves Stock, checks expectedRevision == stock.revision, enforces countedQuantity >= stock.reserved, calculates available = countedQuantity - reserved, atomically updates Stock with revision increment, writes StockMovements with quantity delta

useCases.title: Post financial journal entries
useCases.description: Accountants create and post financial journal entries to the general ledger. The system validates balanced debits and credits using integer minor units, checks currency consistency, and records the posting in the audit trail.
steps: Accountant creates journal entry with debit and credit lines
System validates at least two lines exist with single currency
System calculates total debits and credits using BigInt cents conversion
System validates debits equal credits (balanced journal)
Journal entry is posted atomically with status change from DRAFT to POSTED
Audit event is recorded confirming balanced verification
useCases.evidence: postJournal validates JournalEntries status DRAFT, retrieves JournalLines (minimum 2, single currency), converts debit/credit to BigInt cents, validates exactly one of debit/credit is nonzero per line, calculates sums, enforces debit == credit, atomically updates status to POSTED, writes AuditEvents; cents function parses decimal strings to BigInt minor units with bounds checking

useCases.title: Schedule production and reserve BOM components
useCases.description: Production planners schedule an order using an effective bill of materials and reserve required component stock. The sample validates dates and quantities; it does not implement machine-capacity optimization.
steps: Validate company, plant, production quantity and planned dates
Resolve the effective bill of materials
Reserve component quantities
Create the production order
useCases.evidence: scheduleProduction validates plannedStart/plannedEnd interval, checks Plants and Materials, retrieves BillsOfMaterial where validFrom <= date <= validTo, calculates component.quantity * order.quantity (enforces integral quantities), atomically updates Stock (available -= needed, reserved += needed WHERE available >= needed), writes ProductionOrders (status SCHEDULED) and ProductionComponents (status RESERVED); ZCL_PRODUCTION_POLICY.EVALUATE validates status and yield balancing

useCases.title: Complete production orders
useCases.description: Production planners confirm production completion with actual good and scrap quantities. The system validates yield reconciliation, consumes reserved components, and increases finished goods inventory.
steps: Production planner confirms completion with good and scrap quantities
System validates good + scrap equals planned production quantity
Production order status is transitioned to 'COMPLETED'
Component reservations are consumed and removed from reserved stock
Good quantity is added to available finished goods inventory
Production component status is updated to 'CONSUMED'
useCases.evidence: completeProduction validates goodQuantity + scrapQuantity == order.quantity, transitions ProductionOrders from SCHEDULED to COMPLETED, retrieves ProductionComponents (status RESERVED), atomically updates Stock (reserved -= component.quantity WHERE reserved >= quantity) for each component, updates ProductionComponents status to CONSUMED, updates or inserts Stock for finished material with goodQuantity added to available

useCases.title: Evaluate customer credit for orders
useCases.description: Credit managers evaluate customer creditworthiness during order release. The system calculates credit exposure atomically, applies credit policy, and records credit decisions in the audit trail.
steps: Order release workflow evaluates customer credit
System calculates current exposure and available credit limit
Credit policy is evaluated: exposure + order total <= credit limit
Customer exposure is increased atomically with predicate guard
Credit decision is recorded with exposure before and limit
Order is approved for release or rejected if limit exceeded
useCases.evidence: releaseOrder atomically updates BusinessPartners exposure with predicate (exposure + total <= creditLimit, blocked = false), writes CreditDecisions with exposureBefore/limit/reason; ZCL_ENT_CREDIT.CHECK_ORDER validates order total; ZCL_CREDIT_POLICY.EVALUATE enforces blocked status, amount validation, and limit checks

useCases.title: Monitor and acknowledge operational incidents
useCases.description: Operations managers receive monitoring events from Cloud ALM and other systems, track incident severity, and acknowledge issues. The system ingests normalized monitoring events via webhook and routes them based on severity.
steps: Normalized monitoring event is received from Cloud ALM webhook
System validates event ID format, severity level, and field lengths
Event is deduplicated using external event ID
Incident record is created with source, severity, summary, and correlation ID
Operations manager reviews incident and acknowledges
Acknowledgment is recorded with actor and audit trail
useCases.evidence: ingestMonitoringEvent validates eventID format, severity (INFO/WARNING/CRITICAL), service/summary/correlationID lengths, checks MonitoringEvents for duplicate externalEventID, creates Incidents (status OPEN) and MonitoringEvents; acknowledgeIncident transitions Incidents from OPEN to ACKNOWLEDGED, writes AuditEvents with action INCIDENT_ACKNOWLEDGED

useCases.title: Reconcile operational event logs
useCases.description: System administrators run periodic reconciliation reports to verify that business events match transactional data. The system cross-checks event ledger entries against orders and identifies missing events.
steps: Administrator executes reconciliation transaction or report
System reads order records and event ledger entries
Events are matched to corresponding order records by order ID
Discrepancies are identified where released orders lack events
Reconciliation results are displayed for investigation
useCases.evidence: ZENT_RECONCILE report selects from zent_order and zent_event, loops through orders with status RELEASED, reads event table for order_id, writes discrepancies to output; zcl_hdb_reconcile_delta AMDP procedure calculates ledger-bank deltas for posted transactions

useCases.title: Schedule batch jobs
useCases.description: System administrators schedule periodic batch jobs for reconciliation and other background processing. The system creates job definitions and releases them for execution.
steps: Administrator initiates batch job scheduling
System performs authority check for job release
Job is opened with job name and receives job count
Reconciliation report is submitted to the job
Job is closed and released for immediate execution
useCases.evidence: ZENT_SCHEDULE report performs AUTHORITY-CHECK for S_BTCH_JOB, calls JOB_OPEN to create job, SUBMIT zent_reconcile VIA JOB, calls JOB_CLOSE with strtimmed = abap_true for immediate release

useCases.title: Analyze delivery backlog amounts
useCases.description: Logistics analysts run real-time analytics to calculate the value of orders with delayed deliveries. The system uses HANA SQLScript to aggregate backlog data from orders and deliveries based on planned date and status.
steps: Analyst executes delivery backlog analytical query for company and plant
HANA stored procedure aggregates delivery data with status and date filters
System calculates total backlog quantity where planned date <= as-of date and status is RELEASED or PICKED
Results are returned as aggregated backlog quantity
useCases.evidence: DELIVERY_BACKLOG.hdbprocedure and zcl_hdb_delivery_backlog.clas.abap AMDP both implement identical logic: SUM(CASE WHEN (plannedDate <= asOf AND (status = RELEASED OR PICKED) AND quantity > 0) THEN quantity ELSE 0) filtered by company and plant

useCases.title: Monitor overdue invoices
useCases.description: Collections specialists track invoices that are past due and prioritize collection efforts. The system calculates overdue amounts based on due date, status, and paid amount.
steps: Collections specialist executes invoice overdue analytical query for company and currency
HANA procedure calculates overdue amount for invoices where due date < as-of date
System filters by status (not CANCELLED or PAID) and unpaid balance (amount > paid)
Results are returned as aggregated overdue amount in minor units
useCases.evidence: INVOICE_OVERDUE.hdbprocedure and zcl_hdb_invoice_overdue.clas.abap AMDP both implement: SUM(CASE WHEN (dueDate < asOf AND status NOT IN (CANCELLED, PAID) AND amount > paid) THEN (amount - paid) ELSE 0) filtered by company and currency

useCases.title: Track order exposure and liability
useCases.description: Financial controllers monitor the total value of open sales orders to assess revenue exposure and working capital requirements. The system aggregates unpaid order values by customer and status.
steps: Controller executes order exposure analytical query for company and customer
HANA procedure sums unpaid order amounts where status is RELEASED, SHIPPED, or INVOICED
System calculates exposure as order amount minus paid amount
Results are returned as aggregated exposure in minor units
useCases.evidence: ORDER_EXPOSURE.hdbprocedure and zcl_hdb_order_exposure.clas.abap AMDP both implement: SUM(CASE WHEN (status IN (RELEASED, SHIPPED, INVOICED) AND (amount - paid) > 0) THEN (amount - paid) ELSE 0) filtered by company and customer

useCases.title: Calculate open purchase order value
useCases.description: Procurement analysts calculate the total value of open purchase orders to manage supplier commitments and budget. The system aggregates outstanding purchase order amounts by supplier.
steps: Procurement analyst executes open PO value analytical query for company and supplier
HANA procedure aggregates open purchase order amounts where status is APPROVED or PARTIAL
System calculates outstanding value as (quantity - received) * unit price
Results are returned as aggregated commitment value in minor units
useCases.evidence: PO_OPEN_VALUE.hdbprocedure and zcl_hdb_po_open_value.clas.abap AMDP both implement: SUM(CASE WHEN (status IN (APPROVED, PARTIAL) AND quantity > received AND unitPrice > 0) THEN ((quantity - received) * unitPrice) ELSE 0) filtered by company and supplier

useCases.title: Check product availability for order promising
useCases.description: Order desk representatives check real-time product availability to promise delivery dates to customers. The system calculates available-to-promise quantity based on current stock snapshot.
steps: Representative queries product availability for material and plant
HANA calculation function retrieves maximum available quantity from stock snapshot
System returns available quantity (0 if no stock record exists)
useCases.evidence: AVAILABLE_TO_PROMISE.hdbfunction selects COALESCE(MAX(AVAILABLE), 0) from STOCK_SNAPSHOT where material_ID and plant match input parameters

useCases.title: Analyze released-order exposure by customer
useCases.description: The SQLScript function reads released ORDER_FACT rows for one company and calculates cumulative net order exposure by customer. It does not predict payment dates or read an open-invoice ledger.
steps: Select released orders for the requested company
Partition by customer and order rows by creation time and order ID
Return net order amounts and their cumulative exposure
useCases.evidence: CUSTOMER_CASH_FORECAST uses ORDER_FACT and a partitioned SUM window. Native HANA execution remains unverified.

useCases.title: Assess supplier risk exposure
useCases.description: Supply chain managers assess the risk exposure from suppliers based on delivery performance, defect rates, and lead times. The system calculates a risk score to guide sourcing decisions.
steps: Supply chain manager executes supplier risk assessment query for supplier
HANA calculation function retrieves supplier scorecard metrics
System calculates risk score: (1 - ontime ratio) * 50 + defect ratio * 100 + lead days * 0.2
Default score of 100 is returned if no metrics exist
useCases.evidence: SUPPLIER_RISK.hdbfunction selects COALESCE(MAX((1 - ONTIME_RATIO) * 50 + DEFECT_RATIO * 100 + LEAD_DAYS * 0.2), 100) from SUPPLIER_SCORE where supplier_ID matches input

useCases.title: Monitor enterprise operations through control tower
useCases.description: Operations executives use the control tower dashboard to monitor real-time status of orders, inventory, quality, and incidents. The system provides a unified view through UI5 application consuming OData services.
steps: Executive accesses control tower web application
Dashboard loads real-time KPIs from OData services exposing orders, materials, stock, and incidents
Executive reviews key metrics and exception alerts
Executive drills down into specific areas for detailed investigation
useCases.evidence: Control tower UI5 application declared in controltower webapp Component.js and manifest.json; ControlTower OData service defined in control-tower.cds exposes Orders, Materials, Stock, Incidents views

useCases.title: Maintain and quote effective-dated prices
useCases.description: Maintain company/customer/material prices with validated date ranges and no overlapping periods, then quote an effective price for a requested date and quantity.
steps: Validate organization, amount and calendar dates
Reject overlapping customer/material/currency price periods
Select the effective record and calculate an exact-money quote
useCases.evidence: maintainPrice and quotePrice

useCases.title: Authorize and receive customer returns
useCases.description: Authorize bounded quantities against an invoiced order, then receive the return with restock or scrap disposition and create a credit note with cumulative tax allocation. This does not issue a cash refund.
steps: Validate invoice ownership and remaining returnable quantities
Authorize return lines
Inspect and receive the return with restock or scrap disposition
Create the credit note without over-crediting invoice tax
useCases.evidence: authorizeReturn and receiveReturn

useCases.title: Assign and confirm warehouse picking
useCases.description: Assign one picking task to an actor for an order reservation and require that actor to confirm the exact quantity before shipment.
steps: Assign an existing reservation to a warehouse actor
Reject duplicate assignment for that reservation
Confirm the assigned quantity with the assigned actor
Block shipment while assigned picking remains incomplete
useCases.evidence: assignPicking and confirmPicking; shipOrder picking guard
